transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you for seeing me, I really appreciate it. I, well... I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time with this. 

It's just... I had a bit of an embarrassing moment recently. Nothing too terrible, I hope, but... I was helping out at my volunteer group, and I sort of blew up at one of the younger volunteers. It was just over a crooked tablecloth, of all things. I felt awful right away, because I really don't usually talk to people that way. I try to be a gentleman and treat folks with respect. 

It just really shook me to act like that, so I thought I should come in and make sure I'm doing alright... if that makes sense to you?
Has your irritability or anger been happening more often, or was this the first time you've reacted this way recently?

Well, no, it... it really isn't like me at all. That's why I felt so terrible about it. I mean, I might get a little flustered now and then—who doesn't at my age?—but I'm usually quite even-keeled. 

But lately... I don't know, I guess I have felt a little more on edge than usual. Just small things getting under my skin. But this time, with the tablecloth, it just sort of spilled out. I felt dreadful the moment it happened. I don't want you to think I'm an angry person, Doctor, because I really try my best to be kind to everyone. Do you think it's normal to have a slip-up like that every once in a while?
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, even a little bit, lately?

Well, no, not really. I mean, I still enjoy my volunteer work, and I like to keep my house tidy and read my paper in the mornings. I don't think I've been feeling down, exactly. 

I suppose I might be a little less... enthusiastic some days? But that's just getting older, isn't it? You can't expect a fellow my age to be jumping out of bed with a song and a dance every single day. I still do all the things I'm supposed to do. I hope that's the right answer... I'm trying to be as helpful as I can, Doctor. I just want to make sure I'm not making a fuss over nothing.
Have you been feeling more tired than usual, or like you don’t have much energy, even when doing simple things?

Well, I wouldn't say I'm completely worn out or anything like that. I mean, I still get up and make my breakfast, and I keep the yard looking neat. 

I suppose... maybe by the afternoon, I might feel the need to sit in my chair a bit longer than I used to. But that's perfectly normal for a man of 79, wouldn't you agree? I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around all day doing nothing. I still keep busy. I just... maybe I take things a little slower. That's alright, isn't it? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information, Doctor.
Have you been feeling like you’re not good enough or blaming yourself for things more than usual lately?

Oh, goodness, no. I wouldn't say that at all. I mean... I've always taken a lot of pride in being a decent man, doing my part, you know? Even now, I try to pull my own weight around the house. 

I certainly don't sit around feeling sorry for myself or thinking I'm no good. There's just no use beating yourself up over every little thing, is there? I just try to do what's right and be kind. I hope that's what you're asking... I really don't want to come across as someone who just complains or wallows in self-pity. That's a good way to look at things, don't you think, Doctor?
Have you been feeling unusually worried or anxious about things lately, more than you normally would?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I'm an anxious person. I mean... I try to take things as they come, you know? At my age, you learn pretty quickly that worrying doesn't really fix anything anyway. 

I just go about my day, do my chores, and try to keep a positive outlook. I suppose everyone has a little fret now and then about... oh, I don't know, the state of the world or the weather? But certainly nothing unusual. I try to stay pretty level-headed. I hope that's helpful... I really try my best not to be a bother to anyone with unnecessary fretting. That's the best way to handle things, isn't it, Doctor?
Have you noticed that you’re not getting as much pleasure out of your usual activities as you used to, even slightly?

Well, I wouldn't say that, no. I still enjoy my routine, you know? I like keeping the yard tidy, and I still read my morning paper. 

I suppose... well, maybe I don't spend quite as much time out in the garden as I did a few years back, but I still like looking at it. I think it's just natural to slow down a little and maybe not need as much excitement to be content. I'm perfectly happy just having a quiet day. That's a good way to be at my age, don't you think? I certainly don't want you to think I'm sitting around moping or anything like that. I'm doing just fine, Doctor. Am I giving you the right kind of answers?
Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual, or perhaps feeling restless and unable to sit still lately?

Oh, goodness, no. I wouldn't say I'm restless or... or sluggish, either. I mean, sure, my knees aren't what they were twenty years ago, so I might take my time getting up from my favorite chair, but that's just getting older, isn't it? 

I still get around just fine to do what needs doing. And as for being restless, well, I've always been one to appreciate a good, quiet sit. I don't feel the need to be pacing around or anything like that. I try to just take things at a nice, steady pace. I hope that's the sort of thing you're asking about... I really don't want to sound like I'm falling apart at the seams or making a fuss over nothing. It's better to just keep moving along sensibly, wouldn't you agree, Doctor?

Doctor: Have you noticed feeling down or having a hard time coping emotionally around the time of this incident with the tablecloth or any other recent stressors, even if it was just for a short while?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I've been feeling down. Not at all. I mean, sure, that business with the tablecloth catching fire was... well, it was a bit of a surprise, of course. Anyone would be a little startled by something like that, wouldn't they? 

But I didn't let it get to me emotionally. I just... I cleaned it up, threw the ruined bit away, and that was that. No sense crying over spilled milk, or a scorched table, I always say. I try to keep my chin up and not let those little hiccups bother me. I'm a pretty resilient fellow, I think. I certainly don't want you to worry that I'm not handling things well. I'm coping just fine, really. I hope that's what you were hoping to hear?
Have you found yourself feeling more irritable or easily frustrated in the past week, especially when things don't go exactly as planned?

Well... I suppose I should be completely honest with you, Doctor. I try very hard to be polite to everyone, I really do. But... well, I guess that’s actually what brought me in to see you today. I feel just terrible about it, to be perfectly frank. 

A few days ago, one of the younger volunteers had put a tablecloth on, and it was all crooked. And for some reason... I'm afraid I just blew up at them. I completely lost my temper over it and raised my voice. 

I don't usually talk to people that way, I promise you. I've always prided myself on being a gentleman, and it's not like me at all to make a fuss over something so silly. I suppose I was just a bit more on edge than I realized, but I felt so ashamed afterward. We all have our moments where we get a little frustrated and say things we don't mean, don't we? I really hope you don't think I'm turning into some grumpy old man... I'm usually very even-tempered, I swear.
Doctor: Have you noticed feeling mildly down or having a low mood, even if it wasn't severe, that has been happening more days than not for the past couple of years?

Oh, heavens no. I wouldn't say that at all. I know I just told you about that silly outburst of mine with the tablecloth, but really, overall... I've been quite content these past few years. 

I mean, sure, getting older isn't always a picnic, and we all have our quiet days, don't we? But a low mood lasting for years? No, no. I've always tried to look on the bright side of things. I count my blessings every day, I really do. It just wouldn't be right to complain when I've got a roof over my head and a good life. I try to be a cheerful sort of fellow, generally speaking. I certainly hope I don't come across as a gloomy person to you, Doctor? I always try to bring a smile when I can.
Have you, in the past few months, noticed that you take less pleasure in things you used to enjoy, even slightly?

Oh, goodness, no. I still find a great deal of joy in my day-to-day life. I... well, I like to keep myself busy, you know? I still enjoy tending to my little garden and reading the morning paper, just like always. 

I think it's so important to keep up with the things you love, especially at my age, don't you agree? I certainly wouldn't want to just sit around the house moping. I've always been one to appreciate the simple pleasures, and that really hasn't changed a bit. I hope that's a good sign, Doctor? I'd hate for you to think I was losing my spark.
Have you, over the past two years, experienced days where you felt down or had a low mood, even slightly, and if so, have these days occurred more often than not?

Oh, forgive me, Doctor, I... I think we might have just touched on that a moment ago? Or perhaps I didn't explain myself very well the first time, I'm so sorry if I confused things. 

But no, truly, I haven't had a problem with feeling down over the last two years. Certainly not more often than not. Like I was saying, everyone has a quiet afternoon here and there, but I always make it a point to keep my chin up. I really do try my best to be a positive, upbeat sort of person. 

I hope I'm giving you the information you need? I want to make sure I'm doing this right for you, I'd hate to be a difficult patient.
Over the past two years, have you had days where you felt down or had a low mood, even slightly, and did these days happen more often than not?

Oh, dear... I'm so sorry, Doctor, I feel like I'm making you repeat yourself. I really must apologize if I'm not being clear enough. 

But no, I... I haven't had that problem. Not at all. I've been quite happy, really, these past couple of years. I mean, sure, my bones creak a bit more, but my spirits are good. I always try to find something to smile about every day. I wouldn't want you to worry that I've been walking around with a dark cloud over my head. 

I'm answering these questions alright, aren't I? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful to you.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently, even a little bit?

Oh, no, Doctor, my appetite has been just fine. I... well, I still eat my three meals a day right on schedule. My clothes all fit exactly the same, so I don't believe my weight has changed a bit, either. 

I try to make sure I eat a good, balanced diet—lots of vegetables and such, just like I'm supposed to. I know how important it is to take care of myself at my age, and I really do try to follow all the rules when it comes to my health. 

Does that sound alright to you? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of answers. I just want to make sure I'm being as helpful as possible for your notes.
In the past two weeks, have you felt less interested or less pleasure in doing things, even a little bit?

Oh, heavens no. I still enjoy my usual routine just as much as I always have. I... well, I like to keep myself occupied, you know? Reading the morning paper, doing a bit of tidying up, keeping the house nice and neat. I certainly haven't lost interest in any of that. 

I think it's a terrible shame when folks my age just give up on the things they enjoy, so I make a real effort to stay engaged and keep busy. I wouldn't want to just sit around the house doing nothing all day. 

I hope that's a good thing? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of how I'm doing. Am I being helpful enough for you, Doctor?
Have you noticed that you have to push yourself more to get started on tasks or activities that you used to do without much thought, even slightly more often than before?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that at all. I... well, I've always prided myself on being a self-starter, you know? I get up, make my bed, and get right to whatever needs doing. 

I haven't felt sluggish or needed to force myself to do my daily chores. I like to keep things moving along smoothly. I think it's important to keep up a good work ethic, even when you're retired like me. You can't just let yourself go, can you?

I do hope I'm not sounding too boastful, Doctor. I just want to reassure you that I'm keeping on top of things. Is that the sort of detail you need for your assessment?
Have you noticed that, over the past few months, even small things have been getting under your skin more easily, like they never used to, even if you don't feel down or anxious?

Well... I suppose there was one little incident recently. I... I really don't like to admit it, because it's not how I usually behave at all. I've always tried to be very polite and patient with folks. 

But... I help out down at the community center sometimes, and... well, I ended up raising my voice at one of the younger volunteers. It was just over a crooked tablecloth, of all things. I just... I blew up at them, and it was quite uncalled for. That's actually what made me think I should come in and talk to someone. I don't usually talk to people that way, and I felt just terrible about it afterward. 

I hope you don't think too poorly of me for that, Doctor. I really am trying my best to keep my temper in check. Do you think that's something we can work on? I want to make sure I'm being a good patient for you.
Over the past two years, have you had days where you felt down or had a low mood, even slightly, and did these days happen more often than not?

Oh, goodness no. I... well, I really try to keep my spirits up. These past couple of years, I certainly wouldn't say I've felt down more often than not. 

Sure, everyone has a quiet afternoon here and there, especially at my age, but I've always believed in looking on the bright side. I try to count my blessings every day and just be grateful for what I have. I wouldn't want you to think I'm the sort of person who just sits around feeling sorry for himself. I really do try my best to be positive and pleasant to be around. 

I hope that's a helpful answer for you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need for your notes, Doctor. Am I doing alright with these questions?
